partners.mechanism_chain: ALS2 (HGNC:415) —DISRUPTS→ ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000041); ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000041) —LEADS_TO→ Primary Lateral Sclerosis (HP:0003214); SBF2 (HGNC:10447) —DISRUPTS→ ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000041); ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000041) —LEADS_TO→ Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4B2 (HP:0009752). ALS2 and SBF2 are both critical components or regulators of the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Loss-of-function mutations in ALS2 disrupt this system, leading to the motor neuron degeneration seen in juvenile primary lateral sclerosis. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in SBF2 also disrupt the ubiquitin-proteasome system, contributing to the peripheral neuropathy characteristic of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4B2. The convergence occurs at the level of the shared ubiquitin-proteasome system, impacting cellular protein homeostasis differentially in motor neurons and peripheral nerves.
